title: Security and compliance brief, reference architecture and brief claims shard
story: As the candidate I need a security and compliance brief, a reference-architecture diagram and a sourced claims shard so that I can answer a security-first fintech CTO's first objection with precise facts on Amazon Bedrock and Vertex AI deployment, data handling, certifications, Claude Code controls and how they support FinTechCo's likely obligations, and leave his security team a document they can review.
acceptance: security/security-brief.md exists. After the title, the first content is a three-line executive summary (position, evidence, and the ask of a security review per ADR-005). Sections follow in this order: Deployment patterns and data flow; Anthropic data-handling commitments; Certifications and attestations; Claude Code controls (CC-1..CC-9); Regulatory mapping; Approved statements and do-not-say; Limits and open items; Proposed security review package; 60-second spoken version.

Data-flow table covers Pattern A (Amazon Bedrock in a FinTechCo AWS account) and Pattern B (Vertex AI in a FinTechCo GCP project). Each pattern answers four questions in separate cells: what leaves the laptop or CI runner; where inference runs; what is stored and where; retention and who controls it. Every cell carries a [CLM-4xx] id or a [CLM-?: ...] placeholder, and cross-region or global-endpoint caveats are stated or listed as open items.

Data-handling section states the commercial-terms position on training on customer data, and on retention and zero data retention, exactly as sourced (partial claims use their safeWording). No retention period, percentage or date appears without a [CLM-4xx] id.

Certifications table lists only attestations found on the cited sources, with the entity in scope and the date or report period when the source shows one. Anthropic first-party, AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI are separate sections and no certification is attributed to a party the source does not name. Running grep -inE 'certified|compliant' security/security-brief.md shows only sourced, entity-specific uses or do-not-say rows.

Control catalog has exactly CC-1..CC-9 with the shared names. Each row gives what the control does, its mechanism or setting name as written in the docs, what it does NOT do, the evidence it produces, and a [CLM-4xx] id.

Regulatory table has one row each for: PCI DSS v4.0 (current revision status checked), SOX ITGC change management, GLBA Safeguards Rule, NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500, FFIEC guidance, 2023 interagency third-party risk management guidance, SR 11-7 model risk management for fraud and credit models, fair-lending explainability. Columns: obligation as verified at the primary source with [CLM-4xx]; how Claude Code supports it (CC-n and SD-n ids); what stays with FinTechCo; evidence artefact. Every row says 'supports' and none claims compliance. The section states that FinTechCo's charter, SEC-registrant status and PCI scope are ASSUMPTIONS.
Approved statements table has 8 to 12 one-sentence statements, each with a [CLM-4xx] id and a paired overclaim under 'do not say', so the Narrative team can paste them verbatim.

Product facts are dated 'as of October 2026'. No superlative without a named dated source, no unsourced statistic, price, customer name or quote. Regulated-industry enterprise proof points appear only as a [CLM-?: ...] placeholder pointing to Research range CLM-200..299.

research/claims/trust-brief.json is an array in the claims schema with ids only in CLM-400..449 and at least 25 claims. Each has sources with title, url and publisher (date and excerpt where the source shows them), accessed 2026-10-20 or later, and a safeWording when partial. Every [CLM-4xx] cited in the brief exists in it with status verified or partial.
node org/contracts/validate.mjs passes from the engagement root; citations are written as separate brackets such as [CLM-401][CLM-402].

security/reference-architecture.svg passes xmllint --noout and has viewBox 0 0 1600 900, a title element and a desc element, and no font-size below 16. Text labels name: Developer laptop, CI runner, Claude Code, Amazon Bedrock inside the FinTechCo AWS account, Vertex AI inside the FinTechCo GCP project, and the FinTechCo SIEM or telemetry destination for OpenTelemetry export. Numbered callouts match the CC-n catalog and carry a text label as well as colour. grep -oE 'https?://[^ >]+' on the file lists only the w3.org namespace URL; no script element, @import, logos or cloud-provider marks. The caption reads 'Illustrative reference architecture, as of October 2026'. The brief embeds the SVG with a numbered key.
No secrets, real customer names or Anthropic brand assets: grep -rnE 'sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{12,}' security/ returns nothing.

A handoff is posted to hubs trust and narrative naming the Approved statements section, and a request for enterprise proof points is posted to hub research (node org/cli.mjs hub trust shows the post).
brief:
Write the CTO leave-behind (D7 part 1). Reader: a security-first CTO, 20+ years in financial-services IT, who reads line one of everything and distrusts adjectives; his security team reads the depth. Be precise, hedge exactly where the source hedges, state limits plainly. Mappings say 'how Claude Code supports', never 'makes you compliant'.

Research: load WebSearch and WebFetch (ToolSearch query 'select:WebSearch,WebFetch'). Source order per ADR-006: Claude Code docs (security, permissions, settings, sandboxing, hooks, MCP, monitoring and OpenTelemetry, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, data usage; confirm URLs by fetching), Anthropic Trust Center, commercial terms and privacy or retention pages, AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI data-protection docs, then primary regulatory texts (PCI SSC, NYDFS, eCFR or FTC, FFIEC, Federal Register, Fed and OCC). Never write a retention period, certification, section number or setting name from memory. If the Trust Center will not load (JS portal), source from Anthropic's own pages, mark the claim partial with safeWording, or leave a [CLM-?: ...] and list it under open items. Never carry Anthropic first-party certifications onto the Bedrock or Vertex path, or the reverse.

Check current status before citing: the PCI DSS revision in force, whether SR 11-7 or the CFPB adverse-action circulars were changed or withdrawn, NYDFS 500 amendment dates. Say so if status moved. facts.json is silent on charter, SEC registration and PCI scope: label them ASSUMPTION and turn them into discovery questions in the review package. Proof points belong to Research: use [CLM-?: regulated-industry reference, Research CLM-200..299].

Shared vocabulary with S1-TRU-02, use ids exactly: CC-1 permission modes and allow/ask/deny rules; CC-2 managed settings; CC-3 sandboxing; CC-4 hooks; CC-5 MCP server allowlisting and managed MCP config; CC-6 OpenTelemetry audit export; CC-7 Bedrock or Vertex provider path in the company's own cloud account; CC-8 authentication, SSO and credential handling incl. headless CI; CC-9 data-handling settings (telemetry opt-out, local transcript retention, retention and ZDR terms). FinTechCo SDLC, ASSUMED baseline: SD-1 mandatory human code review; SD-2 CI security scanning; SD-3 branch protection and change management; SD-4 least privilege and secrets management; SD-5 dependency governance; SD-6 logging, SIEM, incident response; SD-7 environment segregation and synthetic data in non-prod.

Claims: own range CLM-400..449 only; never cite another shard's ids; mkdir -p research/claims; do not run org/claims.mjs. SVG: ADR-001 palette, system font stacks, numbered callouts keyed to CC-n. 60-second spoken version: ~150 words, state the word count and time. Target 3,500 to 5,000 words.

notes.text: Carried over from Sprint 1 after the account spend limit; executed player-coach per ADR-007.
